sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 46.6% a year from $6.91 billion in FY2017 to $215.9 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F211].
The window is not a smooth compounder: revenue fell 6.8% in FY2020, was flat at 0.2% growth in FY2023, then rose 125.9% in FY2024, 114.2% in FY2025 and 65.5% in FY2026 [D130][D284][D338][D393][D448].
The FY2024 step change came from Data Center revenue up 217% on Hopper GPU shipments for LLM training and inference [P23][P22].
FY2026 growth was driven by data center compute and networking platforms, with Blackwell the majority of Data Center revenue [P10][P8].
Data Center was 89.7% of FY2026 revenue at $193.7 billion, up 68.2% and contributing 60.2pp of the 65.5% total growth [S56][D620][D621][D622][D448].
Within it, Data Center computing grew 59% on Blackwell demand and networking grew 142% on NVLink for GB200 and GB300 systems [P8].
Operating costs grew 40.7% against revenue growth of 65.5%, so revenue grew 24.8pp faster than operating costs [D468][D448][D476].
Incremental operating margin was 57.3%, and operating income grew 60.1% against net income growth of 64.7% [D475][D449][D450].
Diluted EPS rose 66.7% while the diluted share count fell 1.2%, so per-share growth ran slightly ahead of net income [D452][D470].

Operating margin of 60.4% in FY2026 sits well above the 32.8% window median but below the 62.4% FY2025 high, and gross margin of 71.1% is above its 62.2% median but below the 75.0% high [F50][D813][F49][F30][D819][F29].
The FY2026 operating margin fell 2.0pp, with cost of revenue subtracting 3.9pp, partly offset by R&D adding 1.3pp and SG&A 0.6pp [D463][D477][D478][D479].
The R&D and SG&A effects reflect expense growth driven by compensation, employee growth and compute and infrastructure costs [P5][P4][P9].
In FY2026 net margin of 55.6% sat 4.8pp below the 60.4% operating margin, as other income of $11.1 billion was outweighed by a 15.1% tax rate [F70][F50][D861][X120][D434].
Other income rose on unrealized gains in non-marketable and publicly-held equity securities, including the Intel stake [P3].

Operating cash flow of $102.7 billion was 0.86x net income in FY2026, the window low against a 0.97x median, and free cash flow of $96.7 billion was 0.81x net income [F100][F60][D435][D850][D851][F110][D436].
Free cash flow margin was 44.8%, against a 44.4% window median and a 46.6% FY2025 high [D432][D822][D821].
Capex of $6.04 billion was 2.8% of revenue and 2.13x D&A, up from 1.74x in FY2025 [F105][F10][D431][D437][D382].
Stock-based compensation of $6.39 billion was 6.2% of operating cash flow, down from 7.4% a year earlier [X80][D438][D383].
Total debt was $8.47 billion against $10.6 billion of cash and equivalents in FY2026 [D440][F150].
The pack's net cash figure for FY2026 omits short-term investments, which were not reported that year, so the net-cash comparison across the gap is not on a consistent basis [R3].
The current ratio was 3.91x, below the 4.61x window median but above the 3.52x FY2023 low [F190][D831][D829].
Buybacks of $40.1 billion plus dividends of $974 million came to 42.5% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 1.2% [X150][X160][D444][D470].
Investing cash use rose to $52.2 billion, driven by higher purchases of equity securities and a non-exclusive license agreement with Groq [F120][P1].
Short-term investments were not reported in FY2026 after $34.6 billion in FY2025, so cash and investments and net cash for FY2026 omit them [R3][X188].
This is a disclosure gap rather than a deterioration, but it blocks any clean read of liquidity and net-cash peer rank for the latest year [R3].
Graphics was 44.1% of revenue in FY2023 and fell 25.0% that year [R1][D753][D754].
That decline was a one-period mix shift as Data Center took over the revenue base, and Graphics has since grown 57.0% in FY2026 [D747].
Product revenue members sum to 190% of consolidated FY2026 revenue because some are totals of others [R2].
The overlap limits product-level contribution analysis to the Data Center and Compute lines that reconcile to the segment totals [R2].
Whether gross margin holds above the 71.1% FY2026 level or falls toward the 62.2% window median, reported in the FY2027 10-K [F30][D819].
Whether operating cash flow conversion recovers above the 0.97x window median from the 0.86x FY2026 low, reported in the FY2027 10-K [D851][D850].
Whether Data Center growth stays above the 68.2% FY2026 rate or decelerates, reported in the FY2027 10-K [D621].
